steps.ask: What value must g′(x) take at a turning point, and can this expression ever take that value?
steps.title: Explain why there are no turning points

lines.text: A turning point needs $\hl{1}{g'(x)} = 0$, but the numerator is $-6$, which is never $0$.
Also $(2x-7)^2 > 0$ for every $x$ in the domain ($x \ne 3.5$), so $\hl{1}{g'(x)} < 0$ always.
So $\hl{1}{g'(x)} \ne 0$ for all $x$ in the domain: $g$ has no local maximum or minimum points.

lesson.final: \hl{1}{g'(x)} = -\frac{6}{(2x-7)^2} < 0 \text{ for all } x \text{ in the domain, so there are no turning points}

skill.title: Derive the mortgage repayment formula
skill.input: loan = sum of PVs of repayments

steps.ask: What is one repayment made at the end of period $k$ worth in today's money?
steps.title: Write the loan as the sum of the repayments in today's money

lines.text: A repayment $\hl{2}{A}$ made at the end of period $k$ is worth $\frac{\hl{2}{A}}{(1+i)^k}$ today. Today's value of all $t$ repayments is the loan $\hl{1}{P}$.

steps.ask: What kind of series is this, and which sum formula fits $t$ terms?
steps.title: Use the sum of a geometric series

lines.text: This is a geometric series with first term $a = \frac{\hl{2}{A}}{1+i}$, common ratio $r = \frac{1}{1+i}$ and $t$ terms, so $S_t = \frac{a(1 - r^t)}{1 - r}$.

steps.ask: What is $1 - \frac{1}{1+i}$ as a single fraction?
steps.title: Simplify the denominator

steps.ask: Dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal. What does that give here?
steps.title: Cancel the factor 1/(1+i) and tidy up

steps.ask: What operation clears the fraction on the right, and what then isolates $A$?
steps.title: Make A the subject

lines.text: Multiply both sides by $i(1+i)^t$, then divide both sides by $(1+i)^t - 1$.

lesson.note: The first repayment is paid now, so it is worth $A$ with no discounting, and the last exponent is $t-1$ rather than $t$. The geometric-series method is the same.

steps.ask: Which repayment is made now, and what is a repayment made after $k$ months worth today?
steps.title: Write the loan as the sum of the repayments in today's money

steps.ask: What is the first term, and what is the common ratio between neighbouring terms?
steps.title: Identify the geometric series

lines.text: Geometric with first term $a = \hl{2}{A}$, common ratio $r = \frac{1}{1+i}$ and $t$ terms.
